candidate.title: CIP-TAP
candidate.scope: The lower, independently labeled CIP-TAP workflow in the assigned Illumina schematic: identifying capped small RNA (csRNA) species by staged end-group manipulation, linker ligation, cDNA synthesis, PCR and purification. Its starting material is resolved to the Gu et al. (2012) 18–40 nt small-RNA implementation. The four-class icons and yellow target highlight are explanatory; the separate neighboring CapSeq row and bibliography strip are context. The paper’s unshown CIP-PNK control does not expand this card into a grouped workflow. This record describes the depicted architecture, not all implementations of capped-RNA sequencing.

states.label: Small-RNA fraction containing the capped-small-RNA target and uncapped species
features: The workflow input is labeled csRNA, but visibly contains four chemical classes: 5′ monophosphate (P), 5′ hydroxyl (OH), 5′ triphosphate (PPP) and capped 5′ GPPP RNA.
The matched Gu et al. implementation starts from an 18–40 nt fraction of total RNA; that preparation history explains the small-RNA scope without adding an unshown fractionation operation.
The left-hand repeated four-class icon and yellow highlight identify the capped target. They are descriptive, not a separate material transfer or cap-purification step.

operations.label: CIP
operations.description: Acts on the mixed small-RNA fraction: removes exposed 5′ mono- and triphosphates from uncapped species, producing the 5′-OH class while capped RNA remains capped.
operations.mechanism: Calf intestine phosphatase (CIP), identified in the primary paper, dephosphorylates the uncapped 5′ ends represented in the figure.
operations.information_effect: Reduces subsequent 5′ linker ligation of uncapped RNA while retaining the protected capped target. This is chemical discrimination within a mixture, not physical isolation of capped molecules.

operations.label: 3′ primer ligation and gel purify
operations.description: Adds the depicted teal linker to the 3′ ends of both retained RNA classes and gel-purifies the ligation products. The figure’s caption combines these actions into one stage.
operations.mechanism: The figure calls this primer ligation; the paper identifies the attached material as a 3′ linker. No specific ligase or linker chemistry is assigned from the colored icon.
operations.information_effect: Introduces a common 3′ library interface while preserving the capped-versus-5′-OH distinction. It does not itself select capped RNA.

operations.label: TAP
operations.description: Decaps the capped, 3′-linker-bearing RNA to expose a 5′ monophosphate; the 5′-OH class remains depicted with its 3′ linker.
operations.mechanism: Tobacco acid pyrophosphatase (TAP) removes the cap, yielding the 5′-monophosphate substrate used for the next ligation.
operations.information_effect: Converts prior cap protection into a selectively ligatable 5′ end without adding a new RNA sequence. The cap is lost from the eventual readout carrier.

method_scopes.rationale: The card title and lower-row caption identify CIP-TAP. Every assigned operation follows that row’s connected route. The two retained end-group classes are constituents of the same processed small-RNA sample, as confirmed by the paper, rather than separately prepared workflows. The 3′ and 5′ ligation/gel-purification captions each remain a combined local stage. cDNA synthesis and PCR are separate labeled transformations, with their order supported by the paper. Gu et al. establishes the small-RNA implementation and its preparation history; that inclusion does not assert identical preparation for every broader CIP-TAP use. The neighboring CapSeq row is a distinct method and is not an explicitly depicted alternative within the assigned CIP-TAP row.
